hook: "this app went from $1k/mo to $5k/mo in 7 days f*cling days — and it came from a 2-slide tiktok slideshow"
cta: "i put the entire scaling apps playbook in my free guide (FIRST COMMENT)" — comment-placed lead magnet.
idea: A 2-slide TikTok slideshow (AI visuals + phone-notification copy, app entering naturally) did 1M+ views and 5x'd an app's revenue in 7 days — then scale by making 50 hook/image/notification/CTA variants and ultimately thousands of accounts.
sequencing: Hook: $1K to $5K/mo in 7 days from a 2-slide slideshow (1M+ views).
The recipe: 2 slides, AI visuals, notification copy, natural app entry — 'that's literally it.'
The volume doctrine: 50 versions with different hook/image/notification/CTA.
The mindset: 90% die — marketing is a distribution game.
Bottleneck to endgame: one person can't post 50+/day, so thousands of accounts via creator campaigns.
CTA: free scaling playbook in first comment.
formatting: Case-study + scaling thesis: the money claim, the 4-ingredient recipe (→), the volume doctrine, the distribution endgame. 10s video (direct MP4 via video.twimg.com) + photo; transcript shows no speech — it's a silent slideshow.
why_it_works: Notification-style copy hijacks a Pavlovian reflex — we read notifications. Two slides is the minimum viable story: problem ping → product answer. Silence + text = watchable anywhere.
what_to_steal: The 2-slide notification slideshow as LC's cheapest viral unit: slide 1 = phone-notification-style hook ('Your jewelry is turning your skin green 📲'), slide 2 = LC piece as the natural answer. 50 variants per concept is LC's slideshow batch size.

hook: "TikTok slideshows are one of the easiest organic marketing channels to scale for your app" + 'this app is doing $200K MRR'
cta: none explicit — the agency flex ('u getting left behind') is the close.
idea: Slideshows scale via distribution, not craft: a $200K MRR app runs multi-account slideshow volume; the author's AI-app case did 10M+ views / 6K downloads at $0.43 CPM — thousands of clippers beat a few managed accounts.
sequencing: Hook: slideshows = easiest scalable organic channel; $200K MRR proof.
The callout: 2-4 accounts + a few clippers isn't scalable — headache, no test room, slow learning.
The model: multiple accounts riding distribution power.
The case: AI app, 10M+ views, 6K downloads, $0.43 CPM.
The vision: hundreds of accounts posting daily; thousands of clippers = variations + faster data.
formatting: Scale-pitch: the $200K MRR proof → the overcomplication callout → the 10M-view case → the clipper-army vision. 5s silent video (direct MP4) + photo.
why_it_works: '$0.43 CPM' next to '10M+ views' makes the economics undeniable. The 'you're overcomplicating' frame makes the reader's current effort feel small.
what_to_steal: The $0.43 CPM benchmark for LC's slideshow economics and the 'few accounts isn't scalable' critique — LC's slideshow lane needs hundreds of posting accounts, not a handful. Slideshows as the distribution-first format for LC's fleet.

hook: "this guy just proved slideshows convert way harder than videos 😭"
cta: none explicit — the article link is the CTA.
idea: Slideshows beat videos on conversion because they're easy, cheap, and algo-pushed — the winning move is finding an already-viral replicable format and spamming it.
sequencing: Hook: slideshows convert harder than videos.
The bar: you don't need to kill yourself for $10K MRR.
The one thing: a viral, replicable format.
The formula: find format → build to fit → spam.
formatting: Proof post: the claim → the 3 advantages → the formula (find viral format → build app to fit → spam) → quoted article link. Photo.
why_it_works: 'Convert way harder than videos' is a contrarian claim that demands proof — the quoted article promises it. The 3-bullet advantage list makes slideshows feel like an arbitrage.
what_to_steal: The format-first doctrine for LC's slideshow lane: find the viral slideshow format FIRST, then fit LC's jewelry into it — not the reverse. 'Easy, cheap, algo-pushed' is the slideshow pitch to LC's team.

hook: "You dont need to create one perfect tiktok slideshow but you need to create 100 good ones"
cta: none explicit — the mantra is the content.
idea: Slideshow success is volume × testing: stop overthinking, post 100 good ones, find the winning format, double down, repeat.
formatting: Volume mantra: short lines, 'test, test, test' repetition, two photos.
why_it_works: '100 good ones' gives perfectionists permission to ship. The repetition ('test, test, test' / 'again and again') drills the cadence.
what_to_steal: The 100-good-ones quota as LC's slideshow batch minimum per concept — perfectionism is the enemy; the feed picks winners.

hook: "TikTok slideshows are being used completely wrong."
idea: Slideshows aren't lottery tickets — the real opportunity is direct-response slideshow content engineered to convert, not just go viral.
sequencing: The critique: lottery-ticket posting, recycled hooks, views ≠ money.
The reframe: slideshows as direct response.
formatting: Contrarian take: the lottery-ticket critique → the direct-response reframe → gated playbook. Photo.
why_it_works: 'Completely wrong' creates an instant re-examination — the reader audits their own slideshows. Direct-response framing elevates slideshows from vanity to revenue.
what_to_steal: The direct-response lens for LC's slideshows: every LC slideshow needs a conversion job (save → profile → shop), not just views. 'Views never turn into money' is LC's slideshow QA question.

idea: Noise's Shipaton giveaway challenges brands to post a viral TikTok slideshow from their app's category — slideshows give brands maximum control over creator content.
sequencing: The challenge: a viral slideshow from your app's category.
The pitch: slideshows = maximum brand control.
formatting: Giveaway announcement: 6th #Shipaton, the week's challenge (viral slideshow from your app's category), platform pitch. Photo.
why_it_works: A giveaway manufactures a content wave — the challenge format turns creators into a coordinated fleet for a week.
what_to_steal: The 'maximum control' insight: slideshows are LC's most brand-controllable creator format — script every slide, no filming variance. The giveaway-challenge mechanic is stealable for LC's creator community ('best LC slideshow this week wins $500').

body: The recruitment: TikTok slideshow creators wanted to promote Tails — $1 CPM ($1 per 1,000 views), simple slideshows, paid on views generated, worldwide, no following required.
cta: Implied: apply as a slideshow creator.
idea: Recruiting slideshow creators to promote Tails at $1 CPM — simple slideshows, paid per view, open worldwide, no following required.
sequencing: The terms: worldwide, no following needed.
formatting: Recruitment post: emoji bullets (💰📱💸🌎), the $1 CPM rate, no-following-needed.
why_it_works: 'You don't need a huge following' removes the #1 creator objection. Emoji bullets make the terms scannable in one glance.
what_to_steal: The recruitment template for LC's slideshow fleet: dead-simple gig ('make slideshows'), clear per-view pay, no-following barrier — LC's clipper army onboarding copy.

cta: Implied: apply for the dedicated campaign.
idea: A $1,000 dedicated Tails slideshow campaign for creators ready to post consistently and capitalize.
sequencing: The pay: paid (details cut in file).
formatting: Dedicated-creator recruitment: $1,000 campaign budget, 'push HARD' framing, consistency ask.
why_it_works: 'Dedicated' + 'push HARD' + a named budget attracts serious creators and filters tourists.
what_to_steal: The two-tier creator structure for LC: open $/CPM gigs + dedicated higher-budget tiers for consistent posters — LC's slideshow fleet gets a 'dedicated' track with guaranteed budgets.

idea: Day-16 indie log: warming up TikTok, app approved by Apple, now learning TikTok slideshows — asking how others find great ones.
sequencing: Ask: how do you find great [examples?].
formatting: Day-16 journal: checklist of learnings, the Apple approval win, the slideshow question. Link cut.
why_it_works: Day-counters build a following through cadence; the small win (Apple approval) keeps it human.
what_to_steal: The signal: slideshows are the first format a solo builder learns — lowest barrier to entry confirmed. LC's fleet onboarding starts with slideshows for the same reason.

hook: "962,105 people saved one tiktok hook: 'It's 5am on his birthday'"
cta: "comment HOOKS and i'll DM you the pack 🫡" — gated hook pack.
idea: Save rate beats views as the hook signal — 6 hook types with fill-in templates; the best save rate (6.7%) came from a 1.1M-view video, not the biggest.
sequencing: The data: 6.7% saves beat bigger videos.
The maxim: views = saw, saves = plan to use.
formatting: Data-driven hook taxonomy: 962K-saves opener → 6 types → save-rate insight → gated pack.
why_it_works: 'Views tell you who saw it, saves tell you who plans to use it' reframes optimization.
what_to_steal: Save-rate as LC's slideshow hook metric — optimize for saves (purchase intent), not views. The 6-type taxonomy is LC's hook checklist.

body: The proof: 'post emotional slideshows on tiktok — it's by far the best way to get views; if it's emotional + relatable it will go viral.' One slideshow: 13.3K views, 2,881 likes, 802 shares, 313 saves (TikTok Studio screenshot).
cta: none explicit — the maxim + proof is the content.
idea: Emotional + relatable slideshows are the best view-getter on TikTok — one did 13.3K views / 2,881 likes / 802 shares / 313 saves.
sequencing: The claim: best way to get views.
The proof: 13.3K views, 2.9K likes, 802 shares, 313 saves.
formatting: Maxim + screenshot proof: 3 lines of thesis, TikTok Studio numbers.
why_it_works: 'Emotional + relatable' is a complete creative brief in two words. The Studio screenshot makes small numbers credible.
what_to_steal: The emotional+relatable formula as LC's slideshow creative brief: jewelry slideshows need a feeling (nostalgia, heartbreak, glow-up), not just product shots. The share/save ratio is the quality signal to watch.

body: Two lines total: the claim that emotional slideshows win every time, and that they convert better too.
cta: none explicit — the maxim is the content.
idea: Emotional slideshows outperform every time — and they convert better, not just reach more.
sequencing: The maxim: emotional slideshows do better every time.
The kicker: they convert better too.
The format: two lines, no proof — a thesis stated as fact.
Thread context: part of the author's slideshow scaling series.
formatting: Two-line maxim post: claim → conversion kicker. No media.
why_it_works: 'Every time' + 'convert better' upgrades the claim from reach to revenue — the two words LC cares about most.
what_to_steal: The conversion claim as LC's slideshow north star: LC's emotional slideshows are judged on converts-better, not just does-better.
